payload.name: Preserve candidate facts when merging memories
payload.description: When a construction MERGE combines a new candidate with an existing memory, use the merged content to retain all distinct facts from the candidate, such as donation beneficiaries or organizations.
content: During construction CRUD, when applying a MERGE, compare candidate content with the existing memory and ensure every discrete factual assertion from the candidate appears in the new version.

If the candidate names a donation recipient, cause, organization, or similar affiliation, keep that fact in the merged memory; if the existing memory cannot hold it without losing other key facts, create or update a separate memory for that fact instead of dropping it.

solves: Construction MERGE decisions sometimes collapse a candidate into a related existing memory and accidentally drop a discrete fact that was present in the candidate (here, the donation recipient). Future questions may ask about that dropped fact, so the merged memory must preserve every distinct fact from the candidate. This applies only to CRUD merge operations on construction candidates, not to retrieval or answer generation, and does not require retaining non-factual wording or irrelevant details.
